Naveen Kumar Kashyap Additional District And Sessions Judge Po Mact, South East District, Saket Courts: New Delhi Mact No.: 965/18 Fir no.: 809/2017 Ps :Surajkund, Faridabad, Haryana U/s 279, 337,338 Ipc & 3/181 Mv Act Cnr No.: Dlse01-008526-2018 Deepak Kumar S/o Sh. Fajru R/o Village-Singaar, PS-Punhana, District-Nuh Mewat, Harayana. ............Driver/Respondent no. 1 2. Parveen Jain S/o Sh. Sudarshan Jain R/o H.No. 896, Sec.-22, Faridabad, Haryana Also at: Vpo Abhaypur District-Gurgaon, Haryana ............Registered Owner/Respondent no. 2 Mact No.965/18 Deepak kumar v. Taarif Page No. 1 of 25 Bk 3. New India Assurance Co. Ltd. Connaught House(310400) E-9 Connaught House, 2nd floor, Connaught Circus, New Delhi-01. ......Insurance Company/Respondent no.3. Date of accident : 25.09.2017 Date of filing of Petition : 16.10.2018 Date of Decision : 15.05.2023 Deepak Kumar vs Taarif on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56120983/ 1 Award 1.
texts.facts: A claim petition u/s 166(1) MV Act filed by the claimant/petitioner themselves as per law. 2. As per the claim of the claimants, on 25.09.2017, claimant/injured was going on his motorcycle from his home to Gurgaon via Surajkund, Faridabad road. At about 4.30 pm, when the petitioner reached near MVN chowk, Pali Road, he was hit by offending vehicle bearing no. HR-55T-1525, a TATA Dumper truck which was coming from opposite directions being driven by R-1at a very high speed in contravention of traffic rules and in a rash and negligent manner, as a result of the impact, petitioner sustained grievous injuries in his right leg, right arm and other part of body. Petitioner was taken immediately to Asian Hospital, Faridabad, Haryana and then shifted to Batra hospital, New Delhi. It is further claimed that petitioner remained admitted in hospital for about thirty days and received 80% disability in his right arm and 20% in his right lower leg. 3. Accordingly, FIR u/s 279,337,338 IPC was registered. Even the chargesheet u/s 279,337,338 IPC & 3/181 MV Act filed against the R-1. MACT No.965/18 Deepak kumar v. Taarif Page No. 2 of 25 BK 4. As per record, R-1/driver and R-2/owner filed their reply. In nutshell, it is stated in such reply by R-1&R-2 that no such accident took place by such alleged offending vehicle. It is further stated that at the time of appointment of R-1 as driver by the R-2, R-2 checked his driving licence and also took driving test and after satisfaction, he appointed R-1 as driver on the abovesaid vehicle. It is further stated that award, if any is payable by R-3/insurance company only. It is further claimed that driver/R-1 was having a valid and effective driving licence at the time of alleged accident. 5. Further, reply dated 11.04.2019 filed by insurance company/R-3. In nutshell, it is claimed by R-3 that offending vehicle was insured with such company. But liability of the insurance company is disputed subject to valid driving licence of the R-1 at the time of accident. It is further alleged that there is contributory negligence on the part of the claimant and he himself collided with the offending vehicle. 6. From the pleadings of parties, the following issues were framed by learned Predecessor of this Tribunal on 11.04.2019: 1. Relief. Deepak Kumar vs Taarif on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56120983/ 2 7. Claimant/petitioner examined himself as PW-1. Such PW1 tendered his evidence by way of affidavit as Ex.PW1/A. On MACT No.965/18 Deepak kumar v. Taarif Page No. 3 of 25 BK perusal of such examination in chief by way of affidavit, it can be seen that he deposed on the lines of his original complaint. He relied upon various documents including the discharge summary, MLC, educational certificate and medical bills Ex. PW-1/1 to Ex. PW-1/12. As per record, there is no cross-examination conducted by R-1&R-2 of such witness. In fact, R-1& R-2 did not contested the case regularly. But PW-1/injured was cross-examined at length by learned counsel for insurance company/R-3. 8. No other evidence has been led on behalf of petitioner. 9. Insurance company examined one Rahul Verma, its Assistant Manager in court. Such witness was not cross- examined by petitioner. But, as per record, he was cross- examined on behalf of R- 1&R-2. 10. No other witness was examined by respondent side. 14. In the present case, police after investigation had filed charge-sheet against respondent no.1 under section 279/338 of IPC which is also suggestive of negligence of respondent in causing the accident. Accordingly, the issue No.1 is decided accordingly, in favour of the petitioner. The nature of injuries are grievous and petitioner suffered 90% permanent disability in relation to right upper limb. 2. Non-Pecuniary Loss : (I) Compensation of mental and Rs.25,000/- physical shock : As the petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and suffered 90% permanent disability in relation to right upper limb, he would have undergone great mental and physical shock. (iii) Loss of amenities of life : The Rs.25,000/- petitioner has suffered grievous injuries and suffered 90% permanent disability in relation to right upper limb.

Ltd. vs. Pushpa Rana cited as [2009 ACJ 287], it has been held that the MACT No.965/18 Deepak kumar v. Taarif Page No. 4 of 25 BK negligence has to be decided on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities and a holistic view is to be taken. It has been further held that the proceedings under the Motor Vehicle Act are not akin to the proceedings in a Civil Suit and hence, strict rules of evidence are not applicable. In National Insurance Co. Vs. Pushpa Rana 2009 ACJ 287 Delhi, it was laid down that completion of investigation and filing of chargesheet are sufficient proof of negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle. 15. It may further be noted that in Cholamandlam insurance company Ltd. Vs. Kamlesh 2009 (3) AD Delhi 310, it was held that if driver of offending vehicle does not enter the witness box, an Deepak Kumar vs Taarif on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56120983/ 3 adverse inference can be drawn against him. 21. At this stage, before proceeding further, by rely upon the judgments of C.K. Subramania Iyer v. T. Kunhikuttan Nair, R.D. MACT No.965/18 Deepak kumar v. Taarif Page No. 6 of 25 BK Hattangadi v. Pest Control (India) (P) Ltd. and Baker v. Willoughby which are referred and relied in Raj Kumar Vs. Ajay Kumar & Anr. (2011) 1 Supreme Court cases 343 decided by Hon'ble SC, it can be noted that the provision of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 ("the Act", for short) makes it clear that the award must be just, which means that compensation should, to the extent possible, fully and adequately restore the claimant to the position prior to the accident. The object of awarding damages is to make good the loss suffered as a result of wrong done as far as money can do so, in a fair, reasonable and equitable manner. The court or the Tribunal shall have to assess the damages Deepak Kumar vs Taarif on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56120983/ 4 objectively and exclude from consideration any speculation or fancy, though some conjecture with reference to the nature of disability and its consequences, is inevitable. A person is not only to be compensated for the physical injury, but also for the loss which he suffered as a result of such injury. This means that he is to be compensated for his inability to lead a full life, his inability to enjoy those normal amenities which he would have enjoyed but for the injuries, and his inability to earn as much as he used to earn or could have earned. 22. Further it can be noted that the heads under which compensation is awarded in personal injury cases are the following: Pecuniary damages (Special damages) (i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure. (ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured MACT No.965/18 Deepak kumar v. Taarif Page No. 7 of 25 BK would have made had he not been injured, comprising: (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment; (b) Loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability. (iii) Future medical expenses. Non-pecuniary damages (General damages) (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries. (v) Loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage). (vi) Loss of expectation of life (shortening of normal longevity). 22.1. 22.2. It is only in serious cases of injury, where there is specific medical evidence corroborating the evidence of the claimant, that compensation will be granted under any of the heads (ii)(b), (iii), (v) and (vi) relating to loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability, future medical expenses, loss of amenities (and/or loss of prospects of marriage) and loss of expectation of life. 22.3. Assessment of pecuniary damages under Item (i) and under Item (ii) (a) do not pose much difficulty as they involve reimbursement of actuals and are easily ascertainable from the evidence. Assessment of non-pecuniary damages--Items (iv), (v) and (vi)--involves determination of lump sum amounts with reference to circumstances such as age, nature of injury/deprivation/disability suffered by the claimant and the effect thereof on the future life of the claimant. 22.6. It was observed by Hon'ble Sc in such case of Raj Kumar (supra) that what usually poses some difficulty is the assessment of the loss of future earnings on account of permanent disability--Item (ii) (a). 22.7. Compensation towards loss of income, as noted above is Rs.17,604x3 months = Rs.35,208/- (vi) Cost of artificial limbs (if NA applicable) : MACT No.965/18 Deepak kumar v. Mohanty, learned counsel appearing on behalf of the Appellant, in support of his contentions. Having regard to the prevailing rate of interest and the judgments of Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, including in the case of Erudhaya Priya vs State Express Transport decided on 27 July, 2020, Civil Appeal Nos. 2811-2812 OF 2020 [Arising out of SLP (C) Nos.8495-8496 of 2018], which is Deepak Kumar vs Taarif on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56120983/ 10 three Judges Bench judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court, such interest @ 9% per annum is deemed fit and accordingly granted in the present case. At this stage, it is relevant to the refer to the judgment of A. V. Padma & Ors. Vs., R. Venugopal & Ors. (2012) 3 Supreme Court Cases 378: " ......In the case of Susamma Thomas (supra), this Court issued certain guidelines in order to "safeguard the feed from being frittered away by the beneficiaries due to ignorance, illiteracy and susceptibility to exploitation". In the case of illiterate claimants, the Tribunal is allowed to consider the request for lumpsum payment for effecting purchase of any movable property such as agricultural implements, rickshaws etc. to earn a living. However, in such cases, the Tribunal shall make sure that the amount is actually spent for the purpose and the demand is not a ruse to withdraw money. In the MACT No.965/18 Deepak kumar v. Taarif Page No. 19 of 25 BK case of semi-illiterate claimants, the Tribunal should ordinarily invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. But if the Tribunal is satisfied for reasons to be stated in writing that the whole or part of the amount is required for expanding an existing business or for purchasing some property for earning a livelihood, the Tribunal can release the whole or part of the amount of compensation to the claimant provided the Tribunal will ensure that the amount is invested for the purpose for which it is demanded and paid. In the case of literate persons, it is not mandatory to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. Moreover, in the case of Deepak Kumar vs Taarif on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/56120983/ 12 literate persons, the Tribunal may resort to the procedure indicated in guideline No. (i) only if, having regard to the age, fiscal background and strata of the society to which the claimant belongs and such other considerations, the Tribunal thinks that in the larger interest of the claimant and with a view to ensure the safety of the compensation awarded, it is necessary to invest the amount of compensation in long term fixed deposit. Thus, sufficient discretion has been given to the Tribunal not to insist on investment of the compensation amount in long term fixed deposit and to release even the whole amount in the case of literate persons. This has MACT No.965/18 Deepak kumar v. Taarif Page No. 21 of 25 BK resulted in serious injustice and hardship to the claimants. 55. The following conditions are to be adhered to by SBI, Saket Courts, Delhi with respect to the fixed deposits:- (a) The Bank shall not permit any joint name(s) to be added in MACT No.965/18 Deepak kumar v. Taarif Page No. 22 of 25 BK the savings bank account or fixed deposit accounts of the claimant(s) i.e. the savings bank account(s) of the claimant(s) shall be an individual savings bank account(s) and not a joint account(s).
